question: What is the role of Symfony Flex?

answers.text: A Composer plugin that automates bundle configuration via recipes
A caching layer for Symfony services
A CLI tool to generate Symfony entities
A build system for Symfony assets

explanation: Symfony Flex is a Composer plugin that hooks into the install/update process to automatically apply configuration recipes from the official recipe repository, simplifying package setup.

question: Symfony components can be used independently, outside of the Symfony full-stack framework.

answers.text: Vrai
Faux

explanation: Symfony components are decoupled standalone PHP libraries. They can be used in any PHP project via Composer, without the full framework.

question: Which of the following are kernel events dispatched during a typical Symfony HTTP request? (select all that apply)

answers.text: kernel.request
kernel.controller
kernel.response
kernel.boot

explanation: The main kernel events are: kernel.request, kernel.controller, kernel.controller_arguments, kernel.view, kernel.response, kernel.finish_request, kernel.terminate, kernel.exception. There is no 'kernel.boot' event.

question: According to Symfony's backward compatibility promise, what kind of changes can occur in a minor version (e.g., 7.0 → 7.1)?

answers.text: New features and deprecation of existing ones
Removal of deprecated features
Breaking changes to public APIs
Changes to core service IDs

explanation: Minor versions add new features and may deprecate existing ones, but never break backward compatibility. Deprecated features are removed in the next major version (e.g., 8.0).

question: Which environment variable controls the active environment (dev, prod, test) in a Symfony application?

answers.text: APP_ENV
SYMFONY_ENV
KERNEL_ENV
APP_MODE

explanation: APP_ENV (defined in .env or as a real environment variable) is read by the Runtime component to instantiate the Kernel with the right environment. SYMFONY_ENV was used in older Symfony versions but is no longer the standard.

question: What does the kernel.project_dir parameter contain?

answers.text: The absolute path to the project's root directory
The name of the project as defined in composer.json
The path to the public/ directory
The path to the var/cache directory

explanation: kernel.project_dir is an automatic parameter exposing the absolute path to the project root (where composer.json lives). It is commonly used to build paths to other directories (config/, var/, templates/...).

question: APP_ENV and APP_DEBUG are independent settings: you can run the prod environment with debug enabled, or the dev environment with debug disabled.

answers.text: Vrai
Faux

explanation: Although the dev environment defaults to debug=true and prod to debug=false, they are technically separate variables. You can run prod with debug temporarily enabled to investigate an issue, for example.

question: Which directories belong to the default Symfony project structure? (select all that apply)

answers.text: src/ — application code
config/ — configuration files
var/ — runtime files (cache, logs)
app/ — bootstrap files

explanation: Modern Symfony (since 4.x) uses src/, config/, public/, var/, vendor/, bin/, templates/. The legacy app/ directory was removed when Flex became the default — bootstrap is in public/index.php and bin/console.

question: What is the role of MicroKernelTrait in a default Symfony application?

answers.text: It provides default implementations for registerBundles, configureContainer and configureRoutes inside the Kernel class
It is a lightweight kernel for serverless deployments
It is used only by microservices to skip bundle loading
It replaces the dependency injection container with a smaller one

explanation: MicroKernelTrait removes the need for a dedicated Bundle Extension class by letting the Kernel itself load bundle config and routes from config/packages/ and config/routes.yaml. It is used in default Symfony applications.

question: What does the env var processor json: do, e.g. %env(json:APP_PROVIDERS)%?

answers.text: It JSON-decodes the env var value into a PHP array
It JSON-encodes the env var value to a string
It validates that the env var is a valid JSON string and throws otherwise
It loads a JSON file whose name is given by the env var

explanation: Env var processors transform values resolved at runtime. json: applies json_decode to the env var content, returning an array (or object). Other processors include int:, bool:, base64:, csv:, file:, resolve:, default: and trim:.

question: Which .env-style files are loaded by Symfony at runtime? (select all that apply)

answers.text: .env — committed defaults for all environments
.env.local — machine-specific overrides, ignored by git
.env.prod — committed overrides for the prod environment
.env.shared — shared between several projects

explanation: Symfony loads .env, .env.local, .env.{APP_ENV} and .env.{APP_ENV}.local, in that order of precedence (most specific wins). Real OS environment variables always override these files. There is no .env.shared convention.

question: The symfony.lock file should be committed to the repository to ensure that the same Flex recipes are applied across environments and developer machines.

answers.text: Vrai
Faux

explanation: symfony.lock tracks which Flex recipes have been applied and in which version. Committing it ensures reproducibility — Flex won't reapply or skip recipes inconsistently between checkouts.

question: What is the purpose of config/bundles.php?

answers.text: It declares which bundles are enabled and in which environments
It registers compiler passes for the dependency injection container
It maps bundles to their configuration files in config/packages/
It defines the load order of services for each bundle

explanation: config/bundles.php returns an array mapping bundle classes to environments, e.g. ['Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\FrameworkBundle' => ['all' => true], 'Symfony\Bundle\DebugBundle\DebugBundle' => ['dev' => true, 'test' => true]]. Symfony Flex updates it automatically when packages are installed.

question: What can a Compiler Pass do during container compilation? (select all that apply)

answers.text: Modify or remove existing service definitions
Find services tagged with a given tag and inject them into another service
Add or replace service arguments based on configuration
Execute database migrations before booting the kernel

explanation: Compiler passes run at compile time and operate on ContainerBuilder. They are the primary mechanism to wire tagged services, optimize definitions, or replace classes. They never run at request time and have no access to runtime services like the database.

question: Where is the compiled service container stored at runtime?

answers.text: In var/cache/{env}/ as PHP files (e.g. App_KernelDevDebugContainer.php)
In memory only, rebuilt for each request
In vendor/symfony/cache/
In a SQLite database under var/

explanation: The container is compiled once into PHP files placed in var/cache/{env}/, then included as plain PHP on each request. This makes service resolution extremely fast, with no per-request compilation cost.

question: What does the 'when@env' YAML syntax (e.g. 'when@prod:') allow you to do in a config file?

answers.text: Apply a block of configuration only when the kernel runs in the specified environment
Schedule the configuration block to be applied at a specific time
Mark the configuration as deprecated and removed in a future env
Conditionally enable a bundle based on a feature flag

explanation: The 'when@env' syntax lets you keep environment-specific overrides in the same YAML file as the default configuration, instead of a separate config/packages/{env}/ file. The block is only applied when APP_ENV matches.

question: Real OS environment variables always take precedence over values defined in any .env file.

answers.text: Vrai
Faux

explanation: Symfony's Dotenv component never overwrites variables that are already set in the real environment. This makes it safe to deploy with real env vars in production while keeping .env as a fallback for development.

question: Which of the following typically belong in config/packages/? (select all that apply)

answers.text: framework.yaml — configuration of the FrameworkBundle
twig.yaml — configuration of the TwigBundle
doctrine.yaml — configuration of the DoctrineBundle
routes.yaml — top-level route definitions

explanation: config/packages/ holds bundle configuration files, one per bundle (framework, twig, doctrine, security, etc.). Routing files live in config/routes.yaml or config/routes/, not in config/packages/.

question: What does Symfony Flex actually do when you require a package?

answers.text: It applies a recipe that registers the bundle, generates config files, and updates symfony.lock
It installs the package globally so all projects can share it
It downloads the package source from GitHub and patches it for Symfony
It builds a custom Composer plugin for that package

explanation: Flex is a Composer plugin. When a package has a recipe, Flex applies it: it adds the bundle to config/bundles.php, scaffolds default configuration in config/packages/, may add env vars to .env, and tracks the recipe in symfony.lock.

question: Given the default composer.json mapping "App\\": "src/", which file is loaded for the class App\Entity\User?

answers.text: src/Entity/User.php
src/App/Entity/User.php
src/entity/user.php
vendor/app/entity/User.php

explanation: PSR-4 maps a namespace prefix to a base directory: 'App\' → 'src/'. The remaining namespace becomes the relative path with the class name appended. App\Entity\User → src/Entity/User.php (case-sensitive on most filesystems).

question: When kernel.debug is true, Symfony enables features like detailed exception pages, the web profiler, and Twig's debug functions.

answers.text: Vrai
Faux

explanation: Debug mode enables developer-friendly features that are too costly or insecure for production: rich exception traces, the web profiler/toolbar (when WebProfilerBundle is active), and Twig's debug extension functions like dump().

question: What is the role of public/index.php in a Symfony application?

answers.text: It is the front controller that bootstraps the kernel and handles every HTTP request
It is a static landing page served by the web server
It is generated automatically and should not be modified
It is the entry point only for HTTPS requests

explanation: public/ is the document root exposed by the web server, and index.php is the single entry point: it loads the autoloader and the Runtime component, which instantiates the Kernel and dispatches the Request to it.

question: Which of the following are valid env var processors in Symfony? (select all that apply)

answers.text: bool: — converts the value to a boolean
base64: — base64-decodes the value
default: — provides a fallback if the env var is not set
encrypt: — automatically encrypts the value at rest

explanation: Symfony ships processors for casting and transforming values: int:, bool:, float:, string:, json:, base64:, csv:, file:, require:, resolve:, trim:, default:, const:, url:, query_string:, etc. There is no built-in 'encrypt:' processor.

question: Where is the recommended place to define container parameters that are specific to your application?

answers.text: Under the 'parameters:' key in config/services.yaml
Inside public/index.php before booting the kernel
In a dedicated parameters.yaml file under bin/
In environment variables only — parameters are deprecated

explanation: config/services.yaml has a top-level 'parameters:' section for application parameters. Bundle-specific parameters belong in config/packages/. Parameters are not deprecated, but for values that change between environments you typically read them from env vars.

question: When extending AbstractBundle, what is the purpose of the loadExtension() method?

answers.text: It registers the bundle's services into the container based on the already-merged configuration
It loads PHP extensions required by the bundle (e.g. ext-intl)
It loads compiled translations into memory
It is called only when the bundle is uninstalled by Flex

explanation: AbstractBundle::loadExtension() is the modern replacement for a separate Extension class. Symfony calls it during container compilation with the validated and merged bundle configuration, and you use it to load services and set parameters.
